speaker: Ange Postecoglou
quote_text:
I'd be incredibly proud of your team tonight,  especially what happened in the last game against  
Liverpool, just to get that result and that  performance. Yeah, very proud. And you know,  
again, you know, we had to deal with some  adversity. We started the game really well,  
I thought. But then obviously we lose Cristian  Romero and you know, even in the way it happened,  
it's quite distressing. You see a teammate  go down in that manner and again, you know,  
we had to sort of. Compose ourselves and  deal with that and reorganise. And yeah,  
super proud of the players. I have been all along,  you know, it hasn't been through the one of trying  
that our results haven't been. It's certainly not  been on them. It's just that we just haven't had  
been able to get the consistency to get the  results we needed. But just proud that they  
feel good tonight. They get the rewards of their  hard work, our fans as well, because you know,  
we've put them through a tough time. I thought  they were outstanding tonight. You know,  
we haven't achieved anything, but I think just  that feeling of having a a victory against a top  
opponent in a big game, I think really, really  pleased for everyone. How would you sum up Lucas  
Bergvall's performance in in general,  but also the other side of that about  
the debate around possible second yellow card.  What are your thoughts on that as well? Yeah,  
Lucas is brilliant. I mean, like I said, I haven't  lost sight of the fact that we've got, you know,  
2 x 18 year olds, one who's playing at centre  backs, not even his position. I just don't think  
people really understand, you know, the the the  level of performance that these young guys are  
giving us at the moment. And and you know, we had  a goalkeeper on debut. You know, on debut. Djed's  
playing left back unbelievably well. Um, but  yeah, Lucas, he's just growing all the time. He's,  
you know, he's just got that ability as a  footballer to. To create space for himself,  
he's got the quality, but he works awfully  hard for the team as well. And like I said,  
we've been dealing with some adversity for sure,  but we've had some growth in that. I've got no  
doubt about that. That's been masked by poor  results and poor form for sure. But I've got  
no doubt that when we get our players back, we've  got the foundation of a really sort of, you know,  
strong core group of players we can really grow  with. What happened to Rodrigo Bentancur? Yeah,  
I don't want to speculate, Tom, because  I don't really know either. I mean,  
all I know is he was conscious when he came off.  Obviously it was some sort of head injury, but he  
was conscious when he was coming off the field and  he's been taken to hospital for observation. But  
I'm not really clear on sort of how it happened.  Will you follow up on what happened? Again,  
mate, I don't. It's not my area unless  I, you know, I'll get a doctor out here,  
but I'm not going to speculate because it's just  not fair on people around him. But it was a head,  
head injury and there was concern from players  out there. So obviously there was something going  
on. You gave Antonin Kinsky his debut and threw it  straight in and he had a great performance. Yeah,  
brilliant. Yeah, no, fantastic. You know, I got  the sense when I spoke to him before we signed  
him that he, you know, he had a bit about him in  terms of. you know, a real sort of assuredness,  
you know, and that probably belied his years.  And, you know, we we did, I threw him a mammoth  
task today to play against the best team arguably  in the world at the moment in, you know, in a big  
game, a semi-final, and he just handled it awfully  well. And, you know, I think credit to Johan and  
his team. They They were really big on him as as  a footballer that's going to fit our Our style,  
they they worked really hard to make it happen  now and you can see why he's he's an outstanding  
footballer. Ange, it was a lovely moment  for Lucas, but maybe just seconds earlier  
he could have been sent off. I wouldn't put it in  because Arne spoke about it as well. Yeah, look,  
I spoke about it after the game last time. I think  that my comments were misinterpreted. I I didn't  
criticise the referee on the decision. I didn't  think the decision was right about the handball,  
but that I I said that. It's very hard at  the moment. It's very confusing to understand  
certain elements of the game. Now we've been told  consistently the last few weeks because I've been,  
you know, screaming out from the sidelines because  a lot of teams have got away with a lot of fouls  
with us without bookings because the referee plays  advantage. And we've been told consistently if  
we play advantage, as long as it's not a cynical  foul, then the player does not get cautioned. So  
that that's been relayed to us on a weekly basis  cause we feel like that's been happening. That  
was one of the things I was kinda, you know,  bemoaning last week and there was, you know,  
certain players who just repeatedly were fouling.  We were getting advantage, but no bookings. So  
that's what I'm talking about is that I don't  think and I'm look, I'm really surprised at  
how what's the word I'm looking for, how people  in this country are so. Easily letting the game  
change so much so quickly. It's changed more since  VAR has come in and I've been involved I think in  
the last 50 years. We never used to debate  offsides, we never used to debate handballs,  
we never used to debate holding in the box.  We never used to debate so many things and it  
seems like, I mean did everyone really love the  announcement today? Did that give you real buzz  
about, you know, I mean seriously, but now now I'm  and again look. I understand. My understanding of  
it is, is this is what the people want. That's  what I keep getting told. I understand that. And  
I understand that, you know, we're not gonna.  VAI is gonna be there. Technology is gonna be a  
part of life. But it's like my wife and our kids.  Yeah, we know technology, but she limits screen  
time. Why? You know, we slow things down. I think  we just gotta be be careful about constantly. Why  
do we want to change the game so much? And I  know I'm gonna be the old bloke in the stands  
who keeps shouting Boo every time they argue and  I'll be the only one. But I just thought people  
would be a little bit more protective about the  sanctity of the game. That's what I was talking  
about. I wasn't criticising referees. I wasn't.  I've never criticised. I didn't think the decision  
was right. But it's just the way the game. I  think there's a lot of confusion at the moment.  
That's my belief that the game is changing on  the basis of technology and I'm saying. Why?  
Why isn't anyone like speaking up about it,  especially in this country who, you know, for  
all intents and purposes you feel you guys think  you're custodians of the game. You've got a song  
that says "It's coming home", this is your game,  and yet it takes an Aussie from the other side of  
the world to be the one that's most conservative  about changes. At the minute are those decisions  
like a lottery? Because it feels like in one  game... So my comments "A fair and even playing  
ground". That's what they were about. So today  it it advantaged us. Yeah. I wasn't saying that  
there was a vendetta against me or Tottenham when  I spoke last week. That's not what my comments  
were about. It's just that, you know, and like I  said, I'm and I could be on a lone crusade here,  
but I'm happy to do that. I'm happy to to just be  the lone voice of saying just leave the game alone  
for a bit. Like, you know, even extra time now,  you know, minutes they added on, minutes added  
on there, minutes. We never used to talk about  these things before and yet now everything is  
changing. So that was my. So today I can see why  Arne's would be very disappointed if that was me.  
I'd be disappointed as well. But apparently  they're the rules. So yeah, sorry, but just  
just quickly I want to say that you look  to be a lot more emotional on the sideline.  
During this period that I don't know if I'm  misreading that or that's not how you feel  
or but do you do you that you're conscious of just  letting your emotions out a little bit more. Well,  
yeah. I mean it's been an emotional time mate. You  know it's like I keep saying I am a human being  
you know like all of us you know we're we're in  these roles of of managers and we're supposed to  
you know I understand we've got you know we've got  positions of responsibility but we're still human  
beings in the core. And we react to things and you  know, it's, I don't like the fact that, you know,  
people who are working really hard for this club  on and off the field have not had that feeling of  
victory. I don't feel great about our supporters  not having that feeling of victory. It weighs  
heavily on me, mate. It's my responsibility.  So yeah, you know, I'm a I'm a little bit more  
emotional than I I usually am. But um, you know,  that's, I guess that also probably means I do care  
and I think that's still important. Just a quick  one on Archie Gray and what he's managing through  
every three days and also the relationship he's  building with Radu Drăgușin. It's like I said,  
I I in a position he's never played with, you  know, he's never played an 18 year old. Name me  
another Premier League team that's got two 18 year  olds and one playing out of position consistently.  
It it's I'm so, I'm so happy they're at  our football club and as I keep saying,  
you know. In two or three years time, I just pray  to God I'm the beneficiary of their talent, mate,  
because if somebody else is getting it, I won't  be happy. James, last one, please. Was there any  
change in your sort of overall approach from  the Liverpool game during the league? It felt  
a bit more pragmatic. No, no, you can, you  know, like you can put it that way. I mean,  
people said, you know, my midfield set up was,  you know, a little bit more conservative today.  
That's because I only had three midfielders to  choose, you know, the others weren't available.  
So we certainly went about it the same way. Look,  Liverpool don't allow you to dominate the game  
the way other teams do. And along I said, you  know, we, Ali said, you know, our players every  
three days are playing a game of football, mate,  without rest. And you saw Liverpool at the end,  
they put on some significant talent, some  really good footballers, some top footballers.  
I couldn't do the same. And yet the guys who are  out there are consistently doing it, so. You know,  
maybe we're not as dominant as we wanted to be,  but there's there's good reason, not through  
the lack of trying or, you know, different intent  in terms of how we went about it. OK. Thank you.
title: Ange Postecoglou post-match press conference | Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 Liverpool
